prerequisites: Basic knowledge of algebra and trigonometry
Elements of mathematical analysis: derivation and integration of continuous functions in one real variable

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge of the basic concepts and fundamental laws of classical mechanics and thermodynamics.
Formalize the laws governing the behavior of simple mechanical and thermodynamic systems into equations.
Solve proposed problems as a function of input parameters.
Critically analyze results by checking their consistency using dimensional analysis and numerical accuracy.
Carry out experiments to familiarize with the main problems inherent to the measurement of physical quantities.
Compare measurements with theoretical predictions, evaluating their consistency with respect to the experimental errors.
Use statistical methods to discern between random and potential systematic errors.

syllabus_topics: General concepts on relative motions and reference systems
Linear momentum and impulse theorem, conservation of momentum
Work, kinetic energy, kinetic energy theorem, conservative forces, potential energy, conservation of mechanical energy, energy balance in presence of dissipative forces
Center of mass (CM) and its motion, angular momentum and energy
Work of internal and external forces
Rigid body: moment of inertia, Huygens-Steiner theorem, translational and rotational dynamics
Fluids: pressure, elements of fluid statics and dynamics
Thermodynamics: thermodynamic systems and variables, equilibrium states, equation of state
Thermodynamic cycles, thermal and refrigeration machines
Introduction to kinetic theory of ideal gases
teaching_methods: Use of technological tools (moodle and/or other educational tools, software, videos, quizzes, wooclap)
assessment_rules: The exam usually consists of three parts: midterm and final written exams, a mandatory written laboratory exam, and an oral examination. The oral exam may be waived if either the final written test or both midterm exams are passed with a score above a specified threshold. The minimum scores to waive exams will be communicated via Moodle and in class. Marks are expressed in /30, with the possibility of obtaining a 'cum laude' when a 30/30 mark is exceeded.
